It is zero at t = -1 and t = 0, reaches value -1 at its midpoint, visually centered halfway between -1 and 0, i.e. at t = -0.5. The right plot labeled y(t) shows a triangular pulse above the time axis. It is zero at t = -2 and t = 2, and reaches value +1 at t = 0. Reasoning: To transform x(t) into y(t), the support [-1, 0] of x(t) must map to [-2, 2] for y(t), with the center -0.5 mapping to 0. This is achieved by using the argument (t - 2)/4 = t/4 - 1/2, since t = -2 maps to -1, t = 0 maps to -0.5, and t = 2 maps to 0. Since x(t) is negative while y(t) is positive, the sign is reversed: y(t) = -x((t - 2)/4). Using the CTFT property for x((t - t0)/a), its transform is a X(af)e^{-j2πft0}. Here a = 4 and t0 = 2, so F{x((t - 2)/4)} = 4X(4f)e^{-j4πf}. Including the negative sign gives Y(f) = -4X(4f)e^{-j4πf}.
